title: Twilight Harvest: quick paper + talk harvest (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: capture quick takeaways from recent papers + a 30m talk I watched tonight, map to small experiments we can run with minimal infra friction. Not polished — raw brain-dump for pairing with Ravi/Mina next week.

-- Evening summary (what I consumed) --
1) "Efficient KV Compression for Long-Context Inference" (arXiv, quick skim)
   - Claim: small lossy compression on KV reduces memory by ~3x with <1% perf drop on retrieval tasks. Uses block-wise PCA + inexpensive int8 residuals.
   - My read: interesting for long chat sessions where KV size dominates. Might be brittle on fine-grained token-level recency (few-shot examples).
   - Quick idea: implement prototype encoder that runs as an async post-step on idle worker; compare decode latency vs baseline for 4k/32k contexts.

2) "Adaptive Batch Shaping for Low-P90 Latency" (conference talk, 28m)
   - Key point: shape incoming request batches by prioritizing latency-sensitive routes; small state machine to let high-priority requests preempt batching window.
   - Operational note: this matches our routing SLOs in Console -> per-route latency controls. Could be implemented as a per-route policy in serving runtime.
   - Question: how to surface preemption events to cost dashboard (token accounting fairness)?

3) Blog: "Practical Quantization Tricks for Transformer Heads" (engineering blog)
   - Concrete knobs: per-layer scale factors, clamp schedules during warmup, and the unexpected benefit of bias-correction on head outputs for generation quality.
   - Experiment suggestion: run token-LLR A/B with quantized vs baseline for our curated prompt set (hosted-api model v2). Use Optimize to suggest quant profiles, but we should explicitly track QA degrade by prompt category.

-- Open questions / hypotheses --
- Hypothesis A: block-wise lossy KV compress with occasional full-key snapshots will give 80% memory savings with <2% degradation on instruction-following tasks.
- Hypothesis B: small preemptive windows (5–10ms) reduce P95 on interactive routes by 15% with <3% throughput loss for batchy workloads.
- Hypothesis C: per-head clamp scheduling reduces hallucination in low-bit runs compared to naive quant.

-- Minimal experiments (week-of) --
1) KV compress spike (Ravi + me): prototype a simple PCA-on-chunks encoder in Python; run on recorded 8k chat traces (anonymized) to measure reconstruction token-match and memory reduction. Target: 2-day spike. Linked: github proto issue above.
2) Batch preemption sim (Mina): synthetic traffic generator that mixes latency-sensitive vs batchy clients; implement preemption in local runtime shim (no infra changes) to validate latency/throughput tradeoffs. 3 days.
3) Quant clamp A/B: use Optimize pipeline to propose quant profiles, then run offline generation on curated prompt set (50 prompts across categories). Track LLR and human-rated quality (2 raters). 1 week.

-- Risks / notes --
- KV compress: decoder CPU cost might offset GPU memory gains if we decode frequently; consider lazy decode only on cache hits above threshold.
- Batch shaping: needs careful accounting for cost attribution; could confuse users if billing appears inconsistent. Add explicit trace metadata.
- Quant tests: human labeling is slow; design automatic proxies (LLR, perplexity delta) but default to a small human check.

-- To bring to sync (next Wed) --
- Quick demo: Ravi shows a scatter plot of memory vs token-reconstruction for PCA chunks.
- Mina shows simulated P95 curves with/without preemption.
- I'll draft a short Confluence note summarizing recommended next steps and a proposed feature flag for per-route preemptive batching.

-- Quick links & bookmarks I pulled tonight --
- arXiv:2601.01234 (KV compress)
- talk: Adaptive Batching — youtube link (saved)
- blog: practical quant tricks (engineering.blog/quant-tricks)

-- Closing, fuzzy thoughts --
- Could combine kv-compress with a cache tier: keep recent KVs uncompressed, compress older ones. Might be low-hanging.
- Also want to add small probing suite to Optimize that runs micro-evals for any quant profile change and emits a quality delta. That would close the loop.

Notes to self: remember to anonymize chat traces before sharing; add a line in the Confluence draft about privacy sanitization.

End of dump.
